{{Quote|Those narglatches aren't something I like messing with.|A commoner, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:ac">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=herald|a commoner|Naboo}}</ref>}}
The '''narglatch''', also known as '''narglatch cat''',<ref name="SWE-Talz">{{SWE|groups|talz|Talz}}</ref> was a stealthy apex predator which could be found in diverse environments, such as the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name=":0" /> or the frozen tundras of [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]].<ref name=":1" />

==Biology==
{{Quote|Whenever narglatches come together and start settling down, they only pick a place that's rich in resources.|A commoner, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:ac" />}}
[[File:Narglatch Wildlife.jpg|thumb|240px|A male narglatch on Naboo.]]
The narglatch male had additional fleshy spikes, while females were smoother and slightly smaller. They both had non-retractable claws and a fan-like tail that acted as a rudder during high-speed chases and turns. The narglatch also had densely padded feet that made for silent footfalls.<ref name=":0" />

Males and females only commingled during mating season. Females were more fierce hunters than males, but males could chase a female from her kill. A pregnant narglatch always gave birth to twins, one of each sex. Since young narglatch could hunt immediately upon birth, mothers abandoned them. Cubs hunted together until maturity, making themselves less vulnerable to such fellow predatory Naboo creatures, as [[saw-toothed grank]]s and [[Veermok/Legends|veermoks]].<ref name=":0" /> When food was scarce,<ref name="DB" /> male narglatches would eat young cubs,<ref name=":0" /> so the cubs must ever remain vigilant.<ref name="DB" /> As they approached maturity, the cubs separated.<ref name=":0" /> Older males had longer chin quills.

A solitary hunter, narglatch silently stalked and quickly killed its prey, usually [[muudabok]]s, [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]] or [[jimvu]]. Narglatch generally avoided deep water, although they were capable swimmers should the need arise. One of the few creatures they actively avoided were [[Zalaaca/Legends|zalaacas]].<ref name=":0" /> The younger narglatch cubs preyed on herbivores, swamp and forest-dwellers like [[Ikopi/Legends|ikopi]], while adults could take down bigger prey like [[Fambaa/Legends|fambaa]]. The female narglatch was faster, more agile and the more proficient hunter compared to her male counterpart, able to stalk prey over both land and in water.<ref name="DB" /> They had a remarkable sense of smell that allowed it to track its prey, and formidable night vision.<ref name="Ultimate Adversaries">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Whoohoo&hellip;barely made it out of that one today. I found a whole colony of narglatches nestled up in a cave a ways out. To think I was about to walk right inside and rest for a bit. If you've got nothing left to live for, I can tell you where to find them.|A commoner, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:ac" />}}
[[File:Talz_on_narglatch_mounts.png|thumb|right|240px|Thi-Sen and the Talz colony prepare for war astride narglatches.]]
Found on a number of different worlds, on the frozen [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]] the narglatch were used as mounts by the primitive [[Talz/Legends|Talz]].<ref name=":1">{{TCW|Trespass}}</ref> They were regarded as near-sacred by the Talz, who ride the great cats into battle<ref name=":1" /> and use their bones, meat, and hides for food, shelter, and offerings to the [[spirits of the ice]]. Without them, the Talz would barely survive themselves.

On [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] would ride the sure-footed beasts across their planet and into battle. Though strong and fierce, the narglatch could easily be felled by blaster fire. The Orto Plutonian variety of narglatch<ref name=":1" /> was differentiated from the Naboo<ref name=":0" /> by a mane of fleshy tendrils or protrusions.<ref name=":1" />

Cubs were frequently seen as cute and taken as pets, but became very dangerous as they matured. Escaped narglatches were a threat on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name=":0">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

At least a narglatch was hunted and killed by [[Garnac's hunting guild/Legends|Garnac's hunting guild]]. Its pelt was later placed in their [[Ubrikkian Floating Fortress]].<ref name="Padawan Lost">{{TCW|Padawan Lost}}</ref>

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], packs of narglatches lived in the [[Crystal Cave (Naboo)|Naboo Crystal Cave]]<ref name="SWG:SfaJW">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Jedi|Searching for a Jedi's Weapon|Naboo}}</ref> and in the [[Narglatch Cave]].<ref name="SWG:NC">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=poi|Narglatch Cave|Naboo}}</ref> During that time, the criminals known as the [[Mountain Poachers]] used trained narglatches.<ref name="SWG:CtT">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Commando|Clearing the Trash|Naboo}}</ref> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> the hunter [[Walker Luskeske]] asked a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to kill narglatches in the [[Gallo Mountains/Legends|Gallo Mountains]] on Naboo and bring him fangs as trophies.<ref name="SWG:FaSB">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Find a Security Beacon|Naboo}}</ref> In the meantime, a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] crashed in the Gallo Mountains. [[Tanoa Vills]] requested a spacer to eliminate rabid narglatches, including [[Grizzlefur]], that gathered at the crash site in order to salvage research equipment.<ref name="SWG:StEatCS">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other}}Legacy Quest: "Salvage the Equipment at the Crashed Shuttle" on Naboo</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:NarglatchCubs-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Narglatch cubs hunt [[clodhopper]]s.]]
The narglatch design was first illustrated by concept artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] as a possible creature found on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Based on her artwork,<ref name="DB" /> the narglatch creature was defined as a Naboo native in the video game ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|The Gungan Frontier]]''<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Gungan Frontier'']]</ref> and in the art book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]].''<ref name=":0" /> The narglatch was described in terms similar to large [[Cat/Legends|cat]] predators in our world.<ref name="DB" />
